correctness.rationale: An exact sum over all 16 compatibility graph states in K_2,2 and all 512 states in K_3,3 yields D_2=(q-p)(1-q)(2q^2-q+1) and D_3=(q-p)P(p,q); the two independent maximum-matching algorithms agree on all states. All coefficients of H=-L^8 partial_q P(u/L,(u+v)/L) are nonnegative, with 43 positive and two zero pure-power corners, giving strict negativity of P_q on 0<p<1,p<=q<=1. The independent endpoint identities P(p,p)>0 and P(p,1)<0 imply one and only one crossing. A standalone Python verifier and the full 45-entry coefficient certificate are attached. Exact enumeration proves the polynomial identity for all parameters; numerical checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The saturated OR mechanism models technologies with a ceiling on compatibility improvements, a natural alternative to additive improvements. The theorem determines the minimum balanced market size for a sharp qualitative reversal, proves a unique continuous switching threshold for every 0<p<1, and shows more expected edges can coexist with worse expected optimal match coverage. These three structural features give a motivated design benchmark beyond enumeration for its own sake, while making no unsupported large-market claim.
